title: VoxPulse request scrapbook - raw threads + probe plan
content:
TL;DR: informal roll-up of recent customer threads (mostly mid-market & AI-native). Goal: turn noisy asks into 3 testable probes and 1 micro-product change we can ship in 2 sprints. This doc is deliberately raw — grab snippets for CS playbook or product triage.

Topline themes (quick):
- predictable latency fallbacks: customers want clearer behavior when Hosted API capacity spikes (auto-fallback to cheaper model variants, predictable degraded SLO).
- SDK ergonomics: clearer streaming + function-calling examples for multi-turn apps; customers still patching their own retry/partial-response logic.
- billing transparency: token miscount confusion on batched requests and embeddings vs. generation.
- private deployment onboarding pain: VPC networking checklist and sample terraform is missing or inconsistent.

Raw vignettes / threads (unedited):
1) "High priority for production — we saw a 15s tail on a 1k qps weekend burst. We want an automatic cheap-model fallback (gpt-like->gpt-eco) so our UI doesn't melt. Can you promise X ms or degrade gracefully?" — large fintech customer, support thread 2025-03-10.
2) "Embedding billing spikes us — we batch for throughput but tokens billing seems to double-count. Need a clear statement: are batched embeddings counted per-item or per-total-tokens?" — search-on-doc startup, email 2025-02-28.
3) "SDK streaming examples are fragmented. We hacked a reconnecter for partial responses but it's fragile with tool-calls. Any official pattern?" — mid-market SaaS, slack #cs-demos 2025-03-02.
4) "Private deploy: our infra team expects a terraform module and a checklist for HSM + KMS rotation. The current docs talk at a high level only." — regulated healthcare customer, professional services intake 2025-03-17.

Synthesis notes (quick brain dump):
- Latency/fallback ask is actually an SLO/behavior & product-policy question. Two possible axes: (a) managed fallback policy (auto switch to pinned cheaper variant when latency > threshold) vs (b) observability + recommended configs so customers build their own fallback. Users prefer the managed option if we can guarantee predictable semantics.
- Billing confusion often stems from API surface mismatch between embedding endpoints (per-item vs streaming) and hosting layer batching. Docs + SDK instrumentation could unblock 60% of noise.
- Private onboarding friction is procedural — providing code + checklist (terraform, sample VPC, KMS steps, audit log check) can cut PS time in half.

Candidate micro-probes (pick top 3 to run as experiments):
A) "Fallback policy alpha" (2-week quick): instrument Hosted API to expose a per-route toggle: enable_auto_fallback = true. Behavior: when p50/p95 exceeds X ms or queue depth > Y, route to predetermined cheaper model variant (same output schema). UX: a new header in responses indicating fallback occurred. Success metric: reduction in customer-reported outage tickets by >40% in pilot.
B) "Billing detective" (1-week): ship an SDK helper that logs token accounting per request + demonstrates how batched embedding cost is computed. Include a small runnable notebook. Success: reduce billing confusion threads by half.
C) "Streaming patterns guide + sample reconnect lib" (1 sprint): consolidate patterns for streaming + function-calls; ship a tiny client-side helper that retries incomplete streams and replays tool-calls safely. Measure: CS adoption in 5 pilot customers.

Low-effort deliverable (MVP to ship in 1 sprint):
- Private deploy quickstart: terraform module + README + network diagram + KMS rotation checklist. Package as github repo + Confluence how-to. PS to pilot on 1 customer (healthcare) for feedback.

Open questions / risks (brain-cruft):
- Fallback semantics: do we maintain deterministic outputs for safety/regulatory customers? If not, they will object. Need legal/security POV.
- Cost of auto-fallback: cheaper models may change output quality; need eval harness to detect regressions. Could leverage Optimize evals.
- Billing helper: ensure not leaking token usage sensitive data in logs.

Suggested owner & next steps:
- Product lead: Marco Chen — scope fallback alpha and assign infra/serving-runtime engineer.
- Docs + SDK: Renee Alvarez — short cookbook + notebook for billing detective and streaming patterns.
- PS + private-deploy quickstart: Omar Hassan & Li Wei — assemble terraform bits and run internal dry-run.

Notes to self / workshop prompts for triage meeting:
- Bring one concrete fallback policy option with sequence diagram and sample header payload.
- Prepare a 1-slide risk matrix for fallback (quality, compliance, cost).
- Pull 3 example customer logs demonstrating the latency patterns (need support export).

Slack & ticket refs to grab before triage: #cs-ops thread from 2025-03-09, JIRA-INF-1245 (latency fallback ask), JIRA-CS-934 (billing spike). Also see Confluence voxpulse collection for raw transcripts.

Quick patch ideas (unscoped):
- Add a response header X-Redwood-Fallback: true and a metric tag when fallback triggers (small infra change).
- Add a short FAQ in billing docs explaining token math for batched embeddings (docs + 2 examples).

Closing: this doc is intended to be a working scrapbook. Pull snippets into the CS playbook and product triage board. Flag anything that needs legal/security review asap (fallback semantics + private-deploy HSM).

-- Aisha (notes)
